title: Counts by Status
statement:
Show how many orders are at each stage of delivery, side by side in one row.

The `orders` table has `id` (integer), `customer` (text), and `status` (text, one of `pending`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `cancelled`).

Return one row with three columns: `pending`, `shipped`, and `delivered`, each holding the number of orders with that status. Cancelled orders are not counted anywhere. A status with no orders shows `0`, even when the table is empty.

Expected output:

```text
 pending | shipped | delivered
---------+---------+-----------
       3 |       2 |         3
(1 row)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO orders (id, customer, status) VALUES
  (1, 'Hana Sato', 'delivered'),
  (2, 'Raj Mehta', 'pending'),
  (3, 'Clara Diaz', 'shipped'),
  (4, 'Hana Sato', 'pending'),
  (5, 'Felix Wagner', 'cancelled'),
  (6, 'Raj Mehta', 'delivered'),
  (7, 'Zoe Adams', 'delivered'),
  (8, 'Clara Diaz', 'pending'),
  (9, 'Felix Wagner', 'shipped');

tests.stdin: UPDATE orders SET status = 'delivered' WHERE status = 'shipped';

INSERT INTO orders (id, customer, status) VALUES
  (10, 'Zoe Adams', 'cancelled'),
  (11, 'Omar Khan', 'shipped'),
  (12, 'Omar Khan', 'shipped');

hints: `COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)` counts only the rows that match the condition.
Write one filtered count per status, each with its own column name.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: count only the orders with each status
SELECT COUNT(*) AS pending,
       COUNT(*) AS shipped,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered
FROM orders;
sql.solution:
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending') AS pending,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'shipped') AS shipped,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'delivered') AS delivered
FROM orders;
